newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber - Japan market seen bit firmer, upside limited.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Japan market seen bit firmer, upside limited.

text.p: Japan's rubber futures markets may post a modest technical rebound this week, supported by a firmer spot expiry last Friday and a perception that recent increases in rubber stocks have slowed, traders said on Monday.
But most of the traders added that any potential upswing would be limited as the time was not ripe for a full-fledged recovery because bumper rubber stocks should put a lid on any price rally.
"The market feeling is that sentiment has changed to a slightly bullish side, encouraged by the firmer spot expiry on Friday," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
Traders said a view was starting to emerge that the markets had bottomed out after the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) benchmark hit this year's low of 131.1 yen on October 7.
The newly listed benchmark April contract on TOCOM ended the Monday morning session at 141.2 per per kilo, the same as the opening level.
Similarly, the newly listed benchmark April stood at 141.5 yen in the second morning session, after opening at 141.7 yen.
Traders said slower-than-expected increases in rubber stocks were likely to help the markets post a moderate technical-driven rebound this week.
Stocks at designated warehouses totalled 47,520 tonnes as of October 20, up by 205 tonnes from October 10, the Rubber Trade Association of Japan said.
Although stocks failed to meet a previous estimate of a rise to 50,000 tonnes, one trader said it was too early to say that they had reached their ceiling.
"The upside of 142 yen per kg for the TOCOM benchmark could be hard to break. Market players would be quick to take advantage of any price rebound to sell," one trader said.
The traders also said rain in rubber-producing countries could provide a key for the direction of markets. It rained in Thailand last week and that could hinder tapping.

"If rain in the producing countries is prolonged and disrupts the tapping process, shippers could be wary of selling rubber. If that happens, Japan's rubber stocks could decline," the aforementioned trader said.
The Thai offer price to Japan was quoted at 122 U.S. cents on a free-on-board (FOB) basis as of Monday, flat from last Friday.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber to large-lot end users was quoted at 142 yen per kg on Monday, down from 144 yen on October 21.
